_schema.basis: traceability: source Guidance/Notes sheets, the publication's background information and methodology, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: policyengine-uk's benefit take-up rate parameters cite this DWP publication as their source. Where a PE UK take-up parameter is set from these tables, the comparison is consumed_as_target (agreement partly by construction), not held-out validation. Classify per parameter before scoring; the boundary rule is the same one applied to DWP deductions outturns in issue #21.
annotations.basis: policyengine-uk parameter provenance (gov.dwp take-up parameters); scorecard issue #34 hygiene note

annotations.text: DWP estimates cover Great Britain private households only. PolicyEngine UK simulates the United Kingdom (including Northern Ireland, where equivalent benefits are administered by DfC); a comparable PE counterpart must restrict to GB or annotate the NI wedge.
DWP 'families' are benefit units: a single adult or couple plus dependent children. This matches PolicyEngine UK's benunit entity; counts here are benefit units, not people or households.

DWP caseloads are averaged over the financial year, and take-up compares recipients with those who would receive if everyone claimed for the full period of entitlement. A PE annual-snapshot count is not the same time concept; part-year entitlement drives a wedge.

The entitled non-recipient denominator is simulated by DWP's closed-source PSM on FRS data; the recipient numerator is administrative. Divergence in take-up rates can come from either PE-vs-PSM entitlement simulation or the admin caseload, and the two channels should be decomposed before diagnosis.

Methodological refinements apply from FYE 2017, and the FYE 2024 release adds improved admin-data linking plus calibration-based survey weighting. FYE 2021 is suppressed entirely (COVID). Time-series comparisons across these breaks are not like-for-like; score against the FYE 2024 vintage of each year's estimate, not earlier releases.

Caseloads are rounded to the nearest 10,000, amounts claimed/unclaimed to the nearest £10 million, weekly amounts to the nearest pound, and take-up percentages to the nearest whole point (emitted here as fractions, so precision is ±0.005). Ranges are 95% confidence intervals under a no-non-sampling-error assumption; DWP asks that ranges, not point estimates, be quoted.
annotations.basis: Guidance sheet, Rounding and Accuracy section

annotations.text: From May 2019 both partners in a couple must have reached State Pension age to claim pension-age income-related benefits; mixed-age couples route to UC. Couples rows include one-partner-over-SPa couples until FYE 2019 and both-over-SPa couples from FYE 2020. A PE counterpart must apply the same mixed-age-couple rule per year.

Housing Benefit rows cover pensioner claims only (legacy HB, which persists for pension-age claimants after working-age migration to UC housing element). The PE counterpart is housing_benefit restricted to pension-age benefit units, not all HB and not UC housing support.
